this is marked as a mistake with the rule 'in standard Arabic ḍaghaṭa takes ʿalā', but ضَغَطَ is also transitive in MSA (ضَغَطَ الزِّرَّ is standard and common, e.g. on devices and in dictionaries). Both اضْغَطْ عَلَى الزِّرّ and اضْغَطِ الزِّرَّ are correct; teaching the direct object as wrong teaches an over-strict rule. (Also the 'wrong' form lacks the accusative on الزِّرَّ.)
errors.fix: replace this mistake pair with a real error (e.g. اِضْغَطِي الزِّرّ said to a man → اِضْغَطْ عَلَى الزِّرّ), or soften the why to 'the course uses ḍaghaṭa ʿalā'

summary: Read all 3,091 lines of audit/scenarios-2.txt (16 scenarios: airport-checkin, hotel-reception, job-interview, office-phone, eid-visit, cinema, bank, lost-phone-help, museum-info, post-office, supermarket, phone-shop, dietary, etiquette, machines, school, each with intro, dialogue, mistakes, quiz and photo-scene spots) and checked the Arabic, harakat, case endings, agreement, verb moods, number-noun syntax, translations, seg/tap glosses, answer keys, mistakes pairs and transliteration. The Arabic itself is in very good shape: dual forms (وَالِدَا سَامِي دَعَوَانِي, تُرِيدَانِ أَنْ تَجْلِسَا), diptotes (إِلَى دَنَانِيرَ, لُطَفَاءَ, دَقَائِقَ), numbers (ثَلَاثِمِئَةٍ وَخَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا, عَشْرِ دَقَائِق, اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ جُنَيْهًا), إِنَّ after قَالَ and subjunctives after أَنْ/لَنْ are all correct, every quiz answer key and every mistakes right/wrong pair checks out except one over-strict rule (machines: اِضْغَطِ الزِّرّ treated as wrong). I found 0 major and 15 minor errors: 1 small case-ending slip in a standalone quiz phrase (رَقْمِ التَّتَبُّع), 1 questionable grammar rule, 9 tap-gloss sense mismatches on scene spots and culture notes (the SIM card شَرِيحَة glossed 'slide', سَيِّدَات '(toilets)', حَضْرَة 'sir' for a woman, مَكْتَب/عَرَبَة/رَصِيف/عَمُود/سَاعَة glossed with the wrong sense for the pictured object, أَفْضَلُ 'the best' where it means 'better'), and 4 engine findings (the known 'A / at', 'liāstiqbāl' and 'sh-shāī' quirks plus a new one: wa+li+al / wa+bi+al clusters rendered 'walilrrajuli' / 'Wabiālnnisbati'). The main pattern is that scene-spot tap glosses are drawn from a word-level dictionary and do not always match the object in the photo; the dialogue segs, by contrast, are consistently context-correct. Eight notes cover the صَبَاحَ/صَبَاحُ inconsistency, سُوق gender, photo-location mismatches and minor gloss wording.
